tool_arguments.query: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center spending AI

events.content: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center spending AI

**Microsoft FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending** — for the quarter ended **September 30, 2025**, Microsoft reported **$34.9 billion of capital expenditures**, explicitly attributing the spend to demand for its cloud and AI offerings. [[1]]

- About **half of total capex**—approximately **$17.5 billion**—went to short-lived assets, principally GPUs and CPUs, supporting Azure demand, first-party applications and AI solutions, internal R&D, and replacement of end-of-life server/network equipment. [[1]]
- The other approximately **$17.5 billion** was long-lived infrastructure expected to support monetization for 15 years or more; this included **$11.1 billion of finance leases**, primarily for large data-center sites. [[1]]
- Cash payments for property, plant and equipment were **$19.4 billion**, versus $14.9 billion in FY2025 Q1; the difference between the $34.9 billion capex measure and cash PP&E payments chiefly reflected finance leases and the timing of equipment receipts versus payment. [[1]] [[2]]
- On Microsoft’s cash-flow statement, reported additions to property and equipment were **$19.394 billion**, a **30.0% year-over-year** increase from **$14.923 billion**. [[2]]
- On the broader management capex definition, the **$34.9 billion** was **74.5% higher year over year** than the **$20.0 billion** reported in FY2025 Q1, which also included finance leases. [[1]] [[3]]
- The Q1 figure equaled roughly **44.9% of quarterly revenue** of $77.673 billion, underscoring the unusually capital-intensive nature of Microsoft’s AI capacity buildout. [[4]] [[1]]
- Microsoft also disclosed **$106.2 billion of additional, not-yet-commenced leases**, primarily for data centers, as of September 30, 2025; those leases are scheduled to commence between FY2026 and FY2031. [[5]]
- Management said it planned to increase total AI capacity by **more than 80% in FY2026** and to **roughly double its total data-center footprint over the subsequent two years**. [[1]]
- For the following quarter, Microsoft guided that total capex would rise sequentially and that FY2026 capex growth would exceed FY2025’s growth rate, citing accelerating demand, a growing RPO balance, and increased GPU/CPU spending. [[1]] 

The key analytical distinction is that **$34.9 billion is companywide capex including finance leases**, rather than a pure AI-only or pure data-center number; however, management directly tied the spending mix to cloud and AI capacity, and specifically identified the $11.1 billion f …[truncated]

tool_arguments.query: Alphabet fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

events.content: Alphabet fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

Alphabet spent **$35.7 billion of CapEx in Q1 FY2026** (quarter ended March 31, 2026), with the “overwhelming majority” directed to technical infrastructure supporting AI opportunities. [[1]] 

Within that technical-infrastructure spending, approximately **60% was servers**—including AI compute—and **40% was data centers and networking equipment**; Alphabet did not disclose the technical-infrastructure subtotal, so these percentages should not be applied mechanically to total CapEx. [[1]] 

For FY2026, Alphabet raised CapEx guidance to **$180 billion–$190 billion**, from **$175 billion–$185 billion**, incorporating investment associated with the Intersect acquisition that closed in March. [[1]] 

Management attributed the investment intensity to “unprecedented” internal and external demand for AI compute, while Google Cloud revenue rose **63% year over year** to more than **$20 billion** and backlog reached more than **$460 billion**. [[1]]

Sources:
[S2.1] Alphabet Investor Relations - 2026 Q1 Earnings Call — https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2026/2026-Q1-Earnings-Call-2026-nW8kCrBAKS/default.aspx

tool_arguments.query: Amazon fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

events.content: Amazon fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

**Amazon FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending**

- Amazon’s Q1 FY2026 cash capital expenditure—reported as **purchases of property and equipment—was $44.203 billion**, versus **$25.019 billion** in Q1 FY2025, an increase of **$19.184 billion (76.7% year over year)**. [[1]]
- This is the appropriate reported capex measure for the quarter; it includes broad property-and-equipment spending rather than a separately disclosed “AI data-center” line item. [[1]]
- Amazon said its higher property-and-equipment investment **primarily reflected AI investments**, while its filings show that its relevant infrastructure footprint includes data-center facilities and server/networking equipment. [[2]] [[1]]
- The Q1 outlay represented about **22.1%** of Amazon’s previously stated plan to invest approximately **$200 billion in capex during FY2026**, spanning AI alongside chips, robotics, and low-Earth-orbit satellites. [[3]]
- On a trailing-12-month basis through March 31, 2026, purchases of property and equipment, net of sale proceeds and incentives, were **$147.299 billion**, up from **$87.978 billion** a year earlier; operating cash flow was **$148.531 billion**, leaving **$1.232 billion** in free cash flow. [[1]]
- Amazon therefore does **not** disclose a clean Q1 dollar amount solely for AI data centers; the defensible disclosed answer is **$44.2 billion total quarterly property-and-equipment capex**, with management attributing the overall step-up primarily to AI. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S3.1] amzn-20260331 - Amazon.com, Inc. — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000014/amzn-20260331.htm

[S3.3] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces Fourth Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-Results/

tool_arguments.query: Meta fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

events.content: Meta fiscal year 2026 Q1 capital expenditure data center AI

**Meta Platforms — Q1 FY2026 AI/data-center spending**

- Meta spent **$19.84 billion** of capital expenditures in Q1 2026 (three months ended March 31), including principal payments on finance leases; management attributed this to investments in **servers, data centers, and network infrastructure**. [[1]] [[2]]

- Following the quarter, Meta raised its FY2026 capex outlook to **$125–145 billion**, from **$115–135 billion** previously—an increase of **$10 billion at both ends** of the range. [[1]] [[3]]

- The revised outlook is primarily due to expected **higher component prices**—with management specifically highlighting memory pricing—and, secondarily, incremental **data-center costs** to create capacity for future years. [[3]] [[4]]

- Q1 operating expenses were **$33.4 billion, up 35% year over year**; infrastructure-cost growth reflected higher depreciation, data-center operating costs, and third-party cloud spending. [[3]]

- Meta characterized compute as strategically central to more capable AI models and new products, and said it is expanding its owned data-center footprint, securing component supply, and adding cloud capacity scheduled to come online during 2026 and 2027. [[3]]

- Those multiyear cloud arrangements and infrastructure purchase agreements produced a **$107 billion quarter-over-quarter increase in contractual commitments**, which is a commitment measure rather than Q1 cash capex. [[3]]

**Analyst read-through:** Meta’s Q1 result confirms a substantial acceleration in AI-infrastructure investment, but the FY2026 capex-guide increase was predominantly an **input-cost / component-inflation revision**, rather than solely a new demand-driven buildout; incremental future-capacity data-center spending was explicitly a lesser contributor. [[3]] [[4]]

Sources:
[S4.1] Meta - Meta Reports First Quarter 2026 Results — https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
[S4.2] 1 Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) First Quarter 2026 Results Conference Call — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/META-Q1-2026-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf
[S4.3] META Q1 2026 Prepared Remarks — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/META-Q1-2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
[S4.4] Meta (META) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript - The Globe and Mail — https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/META/pressreleases/1604248/meta-meta-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

**Microsoft FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending** — for the quarter ended **September 30, 2025**, Microsoft reported **$34.9 billion of capital expenditures**, explicitly attributing the spend to demand for its cloud and AI offerings. [[1]]

- About **half of total capex**—approximately **$17.5 billion**—went to short-lived assets, principally GPUs and CPUs, supporting Azure demand, first-party applications and AI solutions, internal R&D, and replacement of end-of-life server/network equipment. [[1]]
- The other approximately **$17.5 billion** was long-lived infrastructure expected to support monetization for 15 years or more; this included **$11.1 billion of finance leases**, primarily for large data-center sites. [[1]]
- Cash payments for property, plant and equipment were **$19.4 billion**, versus $14.9 billion in FY2025 Q1; the difference between the $34.9 billion capex measure and cash PP&E payments chiefly reflected finance leases and the timing of equipment receipts versus payment. [[1]] [[2]]
- On Microsoft’s cash-flow statement, reported additions to property and equipment were **$19.394 billion**, a **30.0% year-over-year** increase from **$14.923 billion**. [[2]]
- On the broader management capex definition, the **$34.9 billion** was **74.5% higher year over year** than the **$20.0 billion** reported in FY2025 Q1, which also included finance leases. [[1]] [[3]]
- The Q1 figure equaled roughly **44.9% of quarterly revenue** of $77.673 billion, underscoring the unusually capital-intensive nature of Microsoft’s AI capacity buildout. [[4]] [[1]]
- Microsoft also disclosed **$106.2 billion of additional, not-yet-commenced leases**, primarily for data centers, as of September 30, 2025; those leases are scheduled to commence between FY2026 and FY2031. [[5]]
- Management said it planned to increase total AI capacity by **more than 80% in FY2026** and to **roughly double its total data-center footprint over the subsequent two years**. [[1]]
- For the following quarter, Microsoft guided that total capex would rise sequentially and that FY2026 capex growth would exceed FY2025’s growth rate, citing accelerating demand, a growing RPO balance, and increased GPU/CPU spending. [[1]]

{"summary":"AI‑related hyperscaler capex (fiscal Q1 2026, latest reported periods):

- **Microsoft** FY2026 Q1 (ended Sep 30 2025): $34.9B total capex; ~$17.5B (~50%) allocated to short‑lived assets (GPUs/CPUs) supporting Azure and AI demand. Source: S1.1, S1.2.
- **Alphabet** FY2026 Q1 (ended Mar 31 2026): $35.7B total capex; ~60% of technical‑infrastructure spend on servers (AI compute) and 40% on data‑center/networking. Source: S2.1.
- **Amazon** FY2026 Q1 (ended Mar 31 2026): $44.2B cash capex (purchases of property & equipment), up 76.7% YoY; management attributed the step‑up primarily to AI investments. Source: S3.1, S3.2.
- **Meta** FY2026 Q1 (ended Mar 31 2026): $19.84B capex (incl. finance‑lease principal); management directed spend to servers, data‑centers, and network infrastructure for AI; FY2026 guidance raised to $125–145B. Source: S4.1, S4.2.

These figures illustrate a strong, coordinated capital‑expenditure surge across the four major cloud/AI operators, signaling robust demand for AI accelerators from both NVIDIA and AMD."}
